newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing sees no signs of higher German CPI.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing sees no signs of higher German CPI.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday the central bank will have to continue fighting inflation with a vengeance, especially because prices may no longer benefit from positive factors next year.
But Issing also said he saw no danger signs indicating a near-term rise in inflation.

Noting Germany's inflation rate will no longer be slowed by low import prices next year, Issing told journalists the Bundesbank "will have to work harder to stay where we are now," referring to inflation levels.
In October, Germany's inflation rate was 1.5 percent.
